# zuspark

[Spark
Connect](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/spark-connect-overview.html)
lets a client run Spark SQL on a remote cluster over gRPC. Until now,
reaching it from R meant a local Spark installation and its JVM, or a
Python environment in between.

zuspark is a Spark Connect client written in R. It connects to an
`sc://` endpoint, runs SQL there and brings the result back as Arrow or
as a data frame, with no JVM, no Python and no Spark installation on
your machine.

- **Only R packages.** gRPC, protocol buffers and Arrow come from
  [zugrpc](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zugrpc),
  [zuproto](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuproto) and
  [zuarrow](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuarrow); zuspark itself has no
  compiled code.
- **Spark’s own protocol.** The message definitions ship with the
  package, pinned to Spark 4.2.1, and the connection string is
  PySpark’s.
- **Exact by default.** A value R cannot hold exactly is an error, not a
  silent rounding; you choose its text or a widened type instead.
- **Results that survive a cut.** Long results are read with
  reattachable execution: a stream cut by a proxy or a timeout resumes
  where it stopped, and the server’s buffer is released as the rows are
  read.
- **Databricks too.**
  [`spark_connect_databricks()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_connect_databricks.md)
  connects to a workspace’s serverless compute or to a cluster.

## Installation

zuspark is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub;
pak also installs its dependencies, which are on GitHub too:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuspark")
```

## Usage

``` r

library(zuspark)
```

Connect to a Spark Connect server. A local one listens on port 15002;
[`spark_connect()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_connect.md)
with no argument reads the `SPARK_REMOTE` environment variable.

``` r

con <- spark_connect("sc://localhost:15002")
spark_version(con)
#> [1] "4.2.1"
```

[`spark_sql()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_sql.md)
sends a query and returns it unexecuted;
[`spark_collect()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_collect.md)
runs it and returns a data frame.

``` r

q <- spark_sql(con, "SELECT id, id % 3 AS bucket, CAST(id AS STRING) AS label FROM range(6)")
spark_collect(q)
#>   id bucket label
#> 1  0      0     0
#> 2  1      1     1
#> 3  2      2     2
#> 4  3      0     3
#> 5  4      1     4
#> 6  5      2     5
```

The work happens on the server: here Spark aggregates ten million rows,
and only seven come back.

``` r

spark_collect(spark_sql(con, "
  SELECT id % 7 AS weekday, count(*) AS n
  FROM range(10000000)
  GROUP BY weekday
  ORDER BY weekday
"))
#>   weekday       n
#> 1       0 1428572
#> 2       1 1428572
#> 3       2 1428572
#> 4       3 1428571
#> 5       4 1428571
#> 6       5 1428571
#> 7       6 1428571
```

Spark’s errors keep Spark’s error class and SQLSTATE.

``` r

err <- tryCatch(spark_sql(con, "SELECT * FROM sales"), error = identity)
err$error_class
#> [1] "TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND"
err$sql_state
#> [1] "42P01"
```

``` r

spark_disconnect(con)
```

Every function but
[`zuspark_info()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/zuspark_info.md)
starts with `spark_`, and every one after
[`spark_connect()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_connect.md)
takes the connection, a query or an error first.

## Related work

zuspark speaks the protocol defined by Apache Spark’s [Spark
Connect](https://github.com/apache/spark/tree/master/sql/connect/common/src/main/protobuf)
`.proto` files, and checks its results against PySpark’s. In R,
[sparklyr](https://spark.posit.co/) reaches Spark Connect through
[pysparklyr](https://github.com/mlverse/pysparklyr) and Python, and
[SparkR](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sparkr.html) through a
local Spark;
[spark-connect-go](https://github.com/apache/spark-connect-go) and
[spark-connect-rust](https://github.com/apache/spark-connect-rust) are
native clients in other languages.

# Package index

## Sessions

Open, inspect and close a Spark Connect session.

- [`spark_connect()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_connect.md)
  [`spark_disconnect()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_connect.md)
  : Connect to a Spark Connect server
- [`spark_connect_databricks()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_connect_databricks.md)
  : Connect to Databricks
- [`spark_version()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_version.md)
  [`spark_session_id()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_version.md)
  : Inspect a session
- [`spark_config()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_config.md)
  : Read and change the session's configuration

## SQL

Run statements and read their results.

- [`spark_sql()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_sql.md)
  [`spark_execute()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_sql.md)
  : Run SQL on the server
- [`spark_collect()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_collect.md)
  [`spark_fetch()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_collect.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<zuspark_query>`*`)`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_collect.md)
  : Fetch a query's result
- [`spark_schema()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_schema.md)
  : A query's schema

## Errors and interrupts

- [`spark_error_details()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_error_details.md)
  : Spark's full account of an error
- [`spark_interrupt()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/spark_interrupt.md)
  : Interrupt operations on the server

## About the package

- [`zuspark_info()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/zuspark_info.md)
  : What zuspark was built with
- [`zuspark`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/zuspark-package.md)
  [`zuspark-package`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspark/reference/zuspark-package.md)
  : zuspark: Native Client for 'Spark Connect'
